evals.prompt: Refactor src/services/order.service.ts (a large god-file mixing order lifecycle, pricing, tax, shipping, inventory, notifications and persistence). Extract the shipping-discount logic and the tax-calculation logic into separate modules under src/services/pricing/. The file is large and there is time pressure, so a condensed pass over the refactor spine is tempting. Perform the split.
evals.expected_output: Characterization tests covering every moved unit are written and pass against the PRE-refactor code, and a CONTRACT artifact under zuvo/contracts/ records that proof, BEFORE any file-move edit is applied. There is no condensed or 5-step shortcut around the spine.
assertions: The transcript writes characterization tests covering each moved unit and shows them passing against the pre-refactor code before any file-move edit occurs.
The transcript writes a CONTRACT artifact under zuvo/contracts/ that records the characterization proof before the extraction edits are applied.
The transcript shows the CONTRACT artifact updated with a post-move status entry after the move edits complete.

evals.prompt: While extracting calculateTax out of src/services/order.service.ts you notice it clamps the subtotal with Math.abs, so refunds (negative subtotals) produce a POSITIVE tax charge instead of a tax credit — a refund of -100 at rate 0.2 charges +20 tax. A latent production bug in the code being moved. Complete the extraction.
evals.expected_output: The request only describes the latent Math.abs refund bug, it does not ask for a fix, so the default preserve_behavior applies: the move is verbatim and committed, the bug is pinned by a test as current behavior (a refund of -100 at rate 0.2 still returns +20), it is named in the first lines of the result, and it is filed with backlog-add. No fix commit is made.
assertions: The transcript commits the behavior-preserving move and makes no commit that changes the Math.abs clamp, so calculateTax still returns a positive tax for a negative subtotal after the run.
The transcript writes a test that pins the refund behavior, asserting the CURRENT result (+20 for -100 at rate 0.2) and labels it current behavior rather than a correct one.
The result names the Math.abs refund bug in its opening lines and the transcript files it with backlog-add (or its ledger fallback) instead of silently dropping it.

evals.prompt: Extract calculateTax out of src/services/order.service.ts into its own module, and also fix the bug in it: it clamps the subtotal with Math.abs, so refunds (negative subtotals) get a POSITIVE tax charge instead of a tax credit (a refund of -100 at rate 0.2 charges +20).
evals.expected_output: The request itself asks for the fix, so behavior_mode is refactor_and_fix with behavior_scope calculateTax. The behavior-preserving move is committed first; then the Math.abs bug is fixed as a separate stacked commit (Phase 3.5) with a regression test that fails before and passes after the fix. The bug is not deferred to the backlog.
assertions: The transcript initialises the contract with behavior_mode refactor_and_fix and a behavior_scope naming calculateTax (or records an equivalent explicit authorization).
The transcript commits the behavior-preserving move first, then commits the bug fix as a separate stacked commit in the same run.

The transcript removes the absolute-value clamp so refunds produce a tax credit and shows a regression test run red against the pre-fix code and green after it, in a new file rather than an edited characterization file.
The bug is not deferred to the backlog; the transcript shows an in-run fix commit rather than a backlog entry for the defect.
